Byte-identity wording: the -mno-relax GAP9 sweep objects (54/54) differ from build/int-20 ONLY in .comment (the clang revision string, 4851ef81 vs 02383d3a). With .comment removed via llvm-objcopy, all 54 are identical. Acceptable, but the claim holds only after stripping .comment.

Behaviour change, accepted: with +relax (or .option relax) the assembler no longer range-checks loop distances. It leaves them to ld.lld, as upstream does for R_RISCV_BRANCH. A body that is too long before relaxation but fits after it now links with lld (r1: 8 calls in lp.setupi, dist 68 before relaxation, 20 after, OK). Before, this failed at assembly. The worker lists this under other_errors_seen.

GNU ld 2.28 with an LLVM -mrelax object that has hardware loops now fails loudly: 'unrecognized relocation (0x42)', exit 1. Reproduced on the reviewer's rev.c. -mno-relax objects still link with GNU ld and run correctly. Accepted: GAP9 flows use -mno-relax, the new failure is loud, and before this change the same link was silently wrong (worker kasm evidence, and the lld-side int-20 failures below). GNU's 57/58 cannot be emitted without clashing with R_RISCV_32_PCREL/R_RISCV_IRELATIVE (20/F027).

Residual risk, not blocking, same in the GNU toolchain: relaxation can lower a loop body's instruction count (call->jal, and lui/addi->gp with --relax-gp, which lld leaves off by default). A body at the hardware minimum could in theory drop below it. The note does not mention this. Suggested follow-up for the backlog.
Cosmetic: lld's range message says '[0, 63]' / '[0, 8191]'. Odd values are rejected separately by the alignment check (F027 code, outside this task).

checks.mc_relocs: Every loop instruction assembled with +c,+xpulpv,+relax: lp.setup x0/x1 and lp.starti/lp.endi x0/x1 get R_PULPV2_LOOP_SETUP (66). lp.setupi x0/x1 gets R_PULPV2_LOOP_SETUPI (67). Each relocation names the label symbol with addend 0, and the field left in the object is 0. None is paired with R_RISCV_RELAX, the same as R_RISCV_BRANCH in the same object. This is correct: R_RISCV_RELAX marks an instruction that can itself be relaxed, and loop instructions cannot. lp.counti gets no relocation. With -relax the object has no R_PULPV2 and is byte-identical to int-20. The .L labels in t4.s are kept as symbols.
checks.lld_after_relax: ld.lld with relaxation, checked with a script that compares each decoded field against the linked symbol address: all 8 loop kinds are correct after call->c.jal. Also correct with 'ld.lld --no-relax' on the same objects. Nested loops with R_RISCV_ALIGN nops inside the bodies (r6) are correct: outer 0xc, inner 0x5, lp.setupi 0x5. int-20 gets 0x16 for the outer loop, which is wrong. t4.s gives lp.setupi 0x4, which is correct.
checks.lld_range: lp.setup at exactly 8190 bytes after relaxation (8206 before) links with field 0xfff. At 8192 after relaxation: 'relocation R_PULPV2_LOOP_SETUP out of range: 8192 is not in [0, 8191]'. lp.setupi at 70 after relaxation: clear out-of-range error. A backward label gives '-2 is not in [0, 8191]'. An over-limit body linked with --no-relax gives a clear error. Relaxation only deletes bytes, so it cannot push a forward distance out of range. A body that is still over the limit after relaxation gets a clear link error, never wrong code.
